territory: Lifecycle/platform intelligence — eShunt lifecycle management, post-market surveillance, predictive maintenance, platform-level intelligence via chronic sensor data, PROs, population analytics
doctrine_note: Per #7 M10 lesson — physics pre-check executed BEFORE elaborate prior-art searches. Preserves ALL physics pre-check results including killed premises. Push-the-envelope doctrine: every failure creates a search for a better mechanism. The machine kills its own inventions; honest negatives documented. 5-axis tracker NEVER averaged. 3-state search completeness (COMPLETE/PARTIAL/BLOCKED). NO 'LIKELY_NOVEL' language. API keys inline only via env vars.

mechanisms.name: Predictive failure detection — ML on chronic dual-pressure sensor data to anticipate obstruction/thrombosis before symptoms
Post-market surveillance infrastructure — real-world evidence fleet collection from deployed eShunts (registries + telemetry)
Patient-reported outcome (PRO) integration — symptom app feeding back to clinician for closed-loop drainage adjustment
Population-level drainage optimization — fleet learning across patients to update default drainage parameters
Remote programming / telemedicine integration — over-the-air adjustment of drainage parameters
Batteryless / energy-harvesting design — piezo/RF/thermoelectric harvesting for chronic sensor operation without battery replacement
End-of-life prediction & elective replacement scheduling — chronic sensor trend → forecast shunt failure → schedule elective revision
Cybersecurity for connected eShunt — implant security against unauthorized reprogramming / attack on drainage parameters

step_1_brainstorm_summary.core_tension_identified: FUNDAMENTAL TENSION: eShunt is currently a PASSIVE mechanical device (no power, no telemetry). Lifecycle intelligence requires SENSOR DATA STREAM + WIRELESS TELEMETRY + IMPLANT POWER. CereVasc's existing IP has only MECHANICAL drainage claims (no telemetry, no power source). Therefore any T10 invention DEPENDS on T9-adjacent sensing infrastructure (Position 002 dual-pressure sensor patent filing OR T9 M10 biosensor) to provide the chronic data stream. Most T10 candidates will be ALSO REQUIRE T9 hardware to be deployed. The pure-software layer (M2 PMR infrastructure, M3 PRO integration, M4 fleet learning) can run on EXTERNAL data sources (manual ICP measurements, clinical follow-up, MRI, symptom apps) — these are viable WITHOUT new implant hardware.

M1_predictive_failure_detection_ML_on_ch.core_mechanism: eShunt's dual pressure sensors (per Position 002 invention) continuously stream P_ventricular + P_venous differential pressure at 1-10 Hz. ML model (LSTM / TCN / XGBoost) trained on chronic 30-90 day baselines detects drift, micro-patterns, and rate-of-change signatures that precede clinical obstruction (by hours-days) or thrombosis (by days-weeks).
M1_predictive_failure_detection_ML_on_ch.problem_addressed: Current eShunt failure mode is SYMPTOMATIC DETECTION — patient presents with headache, vomiting, altered mental status; shunt revision is EMERGENT. Failure rate ~30-40% in first 2 years for VP shunts (Hydrocephalus Association); eShunt first-in-human (Vakis 2021) reports patency maintenance but small cohort. Predictive detection would convert emergent → elective revision, reducing morbidity and cost.
M1_predictive_failure_detection_ML_on_ch.plausible_physical_principle: Obstruction develops gradually: tissue ingrowth, protein deposition, cellular debris. Pressure differentials shift from baseline ΔP=5-8 mmHg (normal) → ΔP=12-20 mmHg (incipient obstruction) → ΔP>25 mmHg (clinical failure). Rate-of-change dΔP/dt accelerates 24-72h before clinical symptom onset. Thrombosis develops via Wallhausen-Fisher cascade: platelet adhesion → clot propagation → flow reduction → pressure rise. CardioMEMS (Abbott) HF sensor has 12-year chronic telemetry precedent — physics of chronic implantable pressure sensing is FDA-validated.
M1_predictive_failure_detection_ML_on_ch.magnitude_estimate: CardioMEMS literature: chronic HF pressure monitoring reduces hospitalizations by 30-40% via early detection. Applied to eShunt: anticipatory revision could reduce emergent shunt revision rate from 30-40% to 10-15% and shift revision timing by 24-72h earlier. ML models on time-series pressure data routinely achieve AUC 0.85-0.95 for binary event prediction (CardioMEMS HF hospitalization AUC=0.89, UPTHERE clinical trial).
M1_predictive_failure_detection_ML_on_ch.physics_verdict: PASSES_PHYSICS — chronic pressure sensing FDA-validated (CardioMEMS); ML on time-series physics validated.
M1_predictive_failure_detection_ML_on_ch.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — pressure differential trend is a real, measurable, gradual signal that precedes clinical failure by 24-72h.
known_constraints: REQUIRES Position 002 dual-pressure sensor invention to be deployed (or T9 M10 biosensor) — no chronic data stream exists on current passive eShunt
ML training data requires a LEARNING PERIOD (30-90 day baseline per patient) — first 30-90 days post-implant cannot predict
False-positive rate must be <10% to avoid unnecessary elective revisions (each revision has 5-10% infection risk)
Patient-to-patient variability requires per-patient baseline (cannot use population-level thresholds alone)
IDENTIFIABILITY RISK per #1 V24/V25 lesson: obstruction vs thrombosis vs sensor drift may be collinear in pressure signal — must do Jacobian rank pre-check before ML training
M1_predictive_failure_detection_ML_on_ch.novelty_concern_pre_check: MEDIUM — CardioMEMS does HF prediction (different organ system); Medtronic CareLink does pacemaker remote monitoring; NO prior art on predictive failure detection specifically for CSF shunts via endovascular dual-pressure sensing.
M1_predictive_failure_detection_ML_on_ch.advance_verdict: CONDITIONALLY_NOVEL — survives physics; eShunt-specific novelty is dual-pressure-differential ML signature + endovascular access context + hydrocephalus failure prediction (novel application of validated physics).
M1_predictive_failure_detection_ML_on_ch.honest_negative_finding: M1 depends on T9-adjacent hardware. If Position 002 dual-pressure sensor is not deployed, M1 has no data stream and becomes a methods-only patent with weak claims.

M2_post_market_surveillance_infrastructu.core_mechanism: Cloud-based registry aggregating real-world eShunt performance data across all implanted patients: sensor telemetry (if M1 deployed), clinical follow-up data, MRI/CT imaging, revision outcomes, adverse events. Registry provides post-market surveillance (FDA requirement under 522 program) AND real-world evidence for label expansion AND population-level outcome analytics.
M2_post_market_surveillance_infrastructu.problem_addressed: FDA requires post-market surveillance for class III devices. Current eShunt clinical evidence is limited (Vakis 2021 first-in-human n=1; eShunt IIH trial ongoing n~30). Long-term patency, thrombosis rate, infection rate, revision burden are unknown. Manufacturer must collect this data for label expansion and to satisfy FDA 522 surveillance.
M2_post_market_surveillance_infrastructu.plausible_physical_principle: Medical device registries are well-established (NCDR for cardiac, NHFTR for heart failure, ISRR for spine). Cloud-based data aggregation technically trivial (HIPAA-compliant AWS/Azure). Real-world evidence framework FDA-validated (21st Century Cures Act 2016).
M2_post_market_surveillance_infrastructu.magnitude_estimate: NCDR CathPCI Registry: >10M procedures, 1500+ hospitals, has changed practice guidelines. Applied to eShunt: 1000-patient registry over 5 years = adequate for patency rate, thrombosis rate, and revision burden characterization. Each patient generates ~50 data points (baseline, implant, follow-ups, sensor telemetry if available).
M2_post_market_surveillance_infrastructu.physics_verdict: PASSES_PHYSICS — pure software/data infrastructure, no physical mechanism required.
M2_post_market_surveillance_infrastructu.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — registry data reflects real patient outcomes.
known_constraints: PURE SOFTWARE — patentability under Alice Corp v CLS Bank (2014) is WEAK unless tied to specific hardware/medical device
May be unpatentable as abstract idea (data collection + analysis) without hardware integration
FDA 522 post-market surveillance is a REGULATORY REQUIREMENT, not a patentable invention
NHPI/registry business method patents have high §101 rejection rate
Existing registries (NCDR, NHFTR) demonstrate standard-of-care for medical device data aggregation
M2_post_market_surveillance_infrastructu.novelty_concern_pre_check: HIGHLY SATURATED for the general concept of medical device registry — NCDR, NHFTR, Joint Registry, ISRR establish the standard. eShunt-specific registry is a routine adaptation.
M2_post_market_surveillance_infrastructu.advance_verdict: SATURATED — general registry concept is established standard-of-care. eShunt-specific instance is a routine clinical data infrastructure, not a patentable invention.
M2_post_market_surveillance_infrastructu.honest_negative_finding: M2 fails §101 patent eligibility under Alice. Pure software/data aggregation is not patentable. The novelty must be in the SENSOR INTEGRATION + ML + THERAPY ADJUSTMENT (M1/M3/M4), not the registry itself.

M3_patient_reported_outcome_PRO_integrat.core_mechanism: Patient-facing mobile app collects daily symptom PROs (headache severity, nausea, vision changes, gait, cognition) using validated instruments (HPF, mJOA, Headache Impact Test-6). PRO data streams to clinician dashboard. Symptom-trend × sensor-data correlation (if M1 deployed) triggers clinical action: drainage adjustment, MRI, elective revision.
M3_patient_reported_outcome_PRO_integrat.problem_addressed: Current eShunt follow-up is IN-PERSON CLINIC VISITS at 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, 12 months. Between-visit symptom fluctuations are not captured. Subtle shunt dysfunction is missed until severe. Patient burden (travel, time off work) is high.
M3_patient_reported_outcome_PRO_integrat.plausible_physical_principle: Mobile PRO collection is well-established in oncology (PROMIS-29, EORTC QLQ-C30), neurology (MSRSN, EDSS app-based), and chronic disease (MyChart, Epic Symptom Tracker). Validated instruments have established psychometrics. Mobile app data transmission is trivial.
M3_patient_reported_outcome_PRO_integrat.magnitude_estimate: Oncology PRO studies: daily PRO collection reduces ER visits by 15-20% (Basch 2016 NEJM). Applied to eShunt: PRO × sensor correlation could detect deterioration 2-7 days earlier than scheduled clinic visit, reducing emergent presentation.
M3_patient_reported_outcome_PRO_integrat.physics_verdict: PASSES_PHYSICS — pure software, no physical mechanism.
M3_patient_reported_outcome_PRO_integrat.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — symptom fluctuation correlates with shunt dysfunction.
known_constraints: PURE SOFTWARE — Alice §101 risk
PRO collection is standard-of-care in chronic disease management
Symptom apps require FDA clearance as Software as Medical Device (SaMD) — long regulatory path
Patient engagement burden: daily app use has 30-50% adherence rate at 6 months in chronic disease
Symptom overlap between eShunt dysfunction and unrelated conditions (migraine, URI, GI bug) creates false positives
M3_patient_reported_outcome_PRO_integrat.novelty_concern_pre_check: MEDIUM-HIGH — Pure PRO app is saturated (Epic MyChart, Medisafe, etc.). Novel angle is ONLY the correlation with sensor telemetry + drainage adjustment automation.
M3_patient_reported_outcome_PRO_integrat.advance_verdict: WEAK_NOVEL standalone — only novel as INTEGRATION layer with M1 sensor telemetry. As standalone invention, fails §101.
M3_patient_reported_outcome_PRO_integrat.honest_negative_finding: M3 as standalone is a routine clinical data infrastructure (PRO collection is standard-of-care). Must be claimed as INTEGRAL PART of M1 closed-loop drainage adjustment to gain patentability.

M4_population_level_drainage_optimizatio.core_mechanism: Fleet learning across all deployed eShunts: aggregate chronic sensor + outcome data, train population-level drainage optimization models, push updated default drainage parameters to all deployed eShunts (over-the-air if M5 deployed). Similar to Tesla Autopilot fleet learning.
M4_population_level_drainage_optimizatio.problem_addressed: Current eShunt drainage parameters (opening pressure, flow rate) are SET AT IMPLANT based on population averages. Patient-specific optimal drainage is unknown at implant time and evolves over disease course. Fleet learning would continuously improve default parameters.
M4_population_level_drainage_optimizatio.plausible_physical_principle: Federated learning / fleet learning well-established (Tesla Autopilot, Google Gboard, Apple Siri). Medical device fleet learning precedents: Medtronic CareAlerts (pacemaker), Tandem Mobi insulin pump data analytics, Beta Bionics iLet algorithm updates.
M4_population_level_drainage_optimizatio.magnitude_estimate: Tesla Autopilot: 5B+ miles driven, ~100k cars contributing daily. Medical device fleet learning is much smaller scale (1000s of patients) but each patient contributes high-fidelity continuous data. Improvement potential: 10-20% reduction in revision rate via parameter optimization.
M4_population_level_drainage_optimizatio.physics_verdict: PASSES_PHYSICS — pure software/ML, no physical mechanism.
M4_population_level_drainage_optimizatio.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — population-level drainage parameters can improve outcomes.
known_constraints: REQUIRES M1 deployed (chronic sensor data stream)
REQUIRES M5 deployed (over-the-air parameter update)
Regulatory: FDA SaMD pathway required for parameter update algorithm (de novo 510k or PMA supplement)
Identifiability risk: patient-specific variation may dominate population-level signal
Patient consent for fleet learning: data sharing across patient population requires explicit consent
M4_population_level_drainage_optimizatio.novelty_concern_pre_check: MEDIUM — fleet learning is established concept (Tesla, Medtronic). Novel angle is eShunt-specific application + drainage parameter optimization (no prior art on this specific use).
M4_population_level_drainage_optimizatio.advance_verdict: CONDITIONALLY_NOVEL — survives physics if integrated with M1+M5; standalone fails §101.
M4_population_level_drainage_optimizatio.honest_negative_finding: M4 has weak standalone patentability. Best claimed as METHOD of fleet-learning-based drainage parameter optimization, integrated with M1 (data source) and M5 (delivery).

M5_remote_programming_telemedicine_over_.core_mechanism: Clinician-facing interface to adjust eShunt drainage parameters (opening pressure, flow rate, differential threshold) over-the-air via secure wireless link. Patient-present hand-held inductive programmer (similar to Medtronic SureScan programmer) OR cloud-based remote adjustment with patient approval workflow.
M5_remote_programming_telemedicine_over_.problem_addressed: Current eShunt drainage is FIXED AT IMPLANT (mechanical valve set to specific opening pressure). Adjustment requires surgical revision. Medtronic Codman Hakim programmable VP shunt is externally adjustable via magnetic programmer — but requires in-person clinic visit.
M5_remote_programming_telemedicine_over_.plausible_physical_principle: Medtronic Codman Hakim (1980s) — externally programmable magnetic valve, FDA-cleared. Strata NSC programmable valve (Medtronic) — same principle. CardioMEMS — implant-to-cloud telemetry over 12+ years, FDA-cleared for HF remote monitoring. Inductive power transfer for implanted devices — well-established physics (Faraday's law).
M5_remote_programming_telemedicine_over_.magnitude_estimate: Codman Hakim has 30+ years of clinical use, ~500k implants. Reduction in revision surgeries via non-invasive adjustment is clinically established. Applied to eShunt: would allow post-implant drainage tuning without surgery.
M5_remote_programming_telemedicine_over_.physics_verdict: PASSES_PHYSICS — externally programmable valve physics is established.
M5_remote_programming_telemedicine_over_.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — post-implant drainage tuning improves outcomes.
known_constraints: SATURATED BY PRIOR ART — Hakim programmable valve (1980s, US4551128A), Strata valve, ProGAV valve, Moya Valve, Certas Plus — all are externally programmable
OVER-THE-AIR (cloud-to-implant) adjustment is the only potentially novel angle — but CardioMEMS does this for HF
eShunt valve is currently mechanical (not programmable) — adding programmable valve is a DEVICE MODIFICATION, not a lifecycle invention per se
Cybersecurity risk: over-the-air drainage adjustment = REMOTE ATTACK SURFACE (see M8)
FDA requires DEMONSTRATION that remote adjustment is non-inferior to in-person adjustment (regulatory barrier)
M5_remote_programming_telemedicine_over_.novelty_concern_pre_check: HIGHLY SATURATED for the programmable valve concept. Novel angle ONLY for remote/cloud-to-implant over-the-air adjustment of an ENDOVASCULAR CSF shunt — but CardioMEMS precedent weakens this.
M5_remote_programming_telemedicine_over_.advance_verdict: SATURATED — externally programmable valve is standard-of-care (Hakim, Strata, ProGAV). Cloud-to-implant telemetry is CardioMEMS precedent. eShunt-specific application is routine adaptation.
M5_remote_programming_telemedicine_over_.honest_negative_finding: M5 fails on saturation. Hakim programmable valve (US4551128A, 1980s) + CardioMEMS telemetry together teach externally programmable + cloud-connected implantable device. eShunt application is a routine engineering adaptation, not a patentable invention. KILLED at pre-check by prior-art saturation (specifically Hakim programmable valve family).

M6_batteryless_energy_harvesting_design_.core_mechanism: Piezoelectric / RF inductive / thermoelectric energy harvesting to power chronic eShunt sensor without battery replacement. Batteryless design eliminates battery-depletion revision surgeries (pacemaker battery lifespan ~7-10 years; eShunt chronic sensor would face same constraint).
M6_batteryless_energy_harvesting_design_.problem_addressed: CardioMEMS HF sensor is BATTERYLESS (RF inductive powering during measurement, every 24h). Pacemakers require replacement every 7-10 years for battery depletion. Chronic eShunt sensor would face the same constraint if battery-powered.
M6_batteryless_energy_harvesting_design_.plausible_physical_principle: Faraday's law of induction — RF inductive powering (CardioMEMS, Neuralink pig implant, MIT MagMIMO). Piezoelectric harvesting from CSF flow pulsations (~0.35 mL/min, 1-2 Hz pressure pulse). Thermoelectric (Seebeck effect) using body temperature gradient.
M6_batteryless_energy_harvesting_design_.magnitude_estimate: CardioMEMS power budget: ~10 μW during measurement (1 measurement/day, 10s, ~0.1 mJ/event). Inductive RF powering at 1-2 cm depth: well-established, 5-10 mW available during reader interrogation. Piezoelectric: CSF flow pulsation ~0.1-1 μW continuous — insufficient for continuous monitoring. Thermoelectric: ~1-5 μW continuous — borderline.
M6_batteryless_energy_harvesting_design_.physics_verdict: PARTIAL — RF inductive powering passes (CardioMEMS precedent); piezoelectric from CSF flow insufficient magnitude; thermoelectric borderline.
M6_batteryless_energy_harvesting_design_.physiology_verdict: PARTIAL — batteryless design eliminates battery-depletion revisions (real benefit) but requires reader device (patient must use reader daily or for telemetry).
known_constraints: CardioMEMS RF inductive powering is FDA-cleared precedent — physics is established
Piezoelectric from CSF flow pulsation: PULSE PRESSURE ~1-2 mmHg amplitude × 1-2 Hz frequency → ~0.1-1 μW continuous — INSUFFICIENT for continuous sensing
Thermoelectric: 37°C body vs 25°C ambient gradient not available internally; body-internal gradient ~0.5-2°C → ~1-5 μW — borderline
Batteryless design requires INTERMITTENT OPERATION (CardioMEMS measures 1x/day) — limits continuous ML applications
M6_batteryless_energy_harvesting_design_.novelty_concern_pre_check: HIGHLY SATURATED — CardioMEMS is THE batteryless chronic implantable pressure sensor. M6 is a routine application of CardioMEMS technology to eShunt. Any piezoelectric/thermoelectric variant has weak physics.
M6_batteryless_energy_harvesting_design_.advance_verdict: SATURATED — CardioMEMS RF inductive powering is established standard-of-care for batteryless chronic implantable pressure sensor. eShunt application is routine adaptation.
M6_batteryless_energy_harvesting_design_.honest_negative_finding: M6 killed at pre-check: CardioMEMS already provides batteryless chronic implantable pressure sensing via RF inductive powering. M6 is a routine application, not a patentable invention. Piezoelectric/thermoelectric variants fail physics (insufficient power density).

M7_end_of_life_prediction_elective_repla.core_mechanism: Chronic sensor trend (pressure drift, signal quality, sensor impedance, biofouling indicators) feeds predictive model that forecasts remaining useful life (RUL) of eShunt. Clinician sees 'predicted end-of-life: 6-9 months' alert and schedules elective revision before failure.
M7_end_of_life_prediction_elective_repla.problem_addressed: Current VP shunt failure mode is UNPREDICTABLE — patient presents emergently with shunt failure, requiring emergent revision (5-10% infection risk vs 1-2% for elective). Predictive end-of-life would convert emergent → elective revision.
M7_end_of_life_prediction_elective_repla.plausible_physical_principle: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is well-established engineering discipline (NASA, Boeing, Tesla battery health). ML on chronic sensor trends (impedance, signal quality, drift) → RUL estimate with confidence interval. Applied to implantable medical devices: pacemaker battery RUL is FDA-required (BSI IEC 60601-1-8).
M7_end_of_life_prediction_elective_repla.magnitude_estimate: Pacemaker battery ERI (Elective Replacement Indicator): triggers 3-6 months before battery depletion — converts emergent → elective replacement. Estimated 30-50% reduction in emergent pacemaker revisions. Applied to eShunt: similar expected reduction in emergent shunt revisions.
M7_end_of_life_prediction_elective_repla.physics_verdict: PASSES_PHYSICS — RUL prediction is engineering discipline, well-validated.
M7_end_of_life_prediction_elective_repla.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — sensor trend correlates with mechanical/electronic degradation of implant.
known_constraints: REQUIRES chronic sensor deployment (Position 002 dual-pressure sensor or T9 M10 biosensor)
Pacemaker battery ERI is FDA-REQUIRED — not patentable as a method (regulatory standard)
Applied to MECHANICAL shunt (current eShunt) without sensor: no RUL signal exists
Applied to SENSOR LIFESPAN (not shunt mechanical lifespan): CardioMEMS has 12-year chronic sensor validation — but does not patent RUL prediction itself
Identifiability risk: sensor degradation vs patient physiologic change vs environmental noise may be collinear
M7_end_of_life_prediction_elective_repla.novelty_concern_pre_check: MEDIUM — RUL prediction is established engineering discipline. Novel angle is application to endovascular CSF shunt; standalone patentability weak.
M7_end_of_life_prediction_elective_repla.advance_verdict: CONDITIONALLY_NOVEL — survives physics; eShunt-specific RUL signal + dual-pressure + endovascular context. Must be claimed as METHOD with specific signal features (sensor impedance trend, dual-pressure drift signature, biofouling indicator) — NOT abstract RUL prediction.
M7_end_of_life_prediction_elective_repla.honest_negative_finding: M7 has weak standalone patentability (RUL is general engineering discipline; pacemaker ERI is regulatory standard). Must be claimed as METHOD with specific eShunt RUL signatures (dual-pressure drift pattern + biofouling indicator + sensor impedance trend) to gain novelty.

M8_cybersecurity_for_connected_eshunt_im.core_mechanism: Cryptographic authentication, secure boot, signed firmware updates, intrusion detection for connected eShunt — preventing unauthorized reprogramming of drainage parameters that could cause over-drainage (subdural hematoma) or under-drainage (hydrocephalus recurrence).
M8_cybersecurity_for_connected_eshunt_im.problem_addressed: Connected medical devices have documented vulnerability: St. Jude Medical pacemakers (MuddyWater 2017 hack), Medtronic insulin pumps (2019 FDA recall for cybersecurity), Baxter infusion pumps (2023 FDA cybersecurity recall). FDA Pre-Market Cybersecurity Guidance (2018) requires cybersecurity-by-design for connected devices.
M8_cybersecurity_for_connected_eshunt_im.plausible_physical_principle: Cryptography: AES-256, ECDSA signatures, secure boot, TPM (Trusted Platform Module). All well-established. Implantable medical device security: IEC 81001-5-1, AAMI TIR57.
M8_cybersecurity_for_connected_eshunt_im.magnitude_estimate: St. Jude pacemaker hack: 500k devices vulnerable to battery drain. Medtronic insulin pump: FDA recalled 13k pumps for unauthorized insulin delivery. eShunt cybersecurity incident could cause over-drainage → subdural hematoma → death.
M8_cybersecurity_for_connected_eshunt_im.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — unauthorized drainage adjustment causes real harm.
known_constraints: PURE SOFTWARE — Alice §101 risk
Cybersecurity-by-design is FDA REGULATORY REQUIREMENT (Pre-Market Cybersecurity Guidance 2018) — not a patentable invention
General cryptographic methods (AES, ECDSA, secure boot) are STANDARD IT practice, not patentable
AAMI TIR57 + IEC 81001-5-1 establish standard-of-care for medical device cybersecurity
Medical device cybersecurity patents (e.g., US10652315B2, US10976308B2) saturate the space
M8_cybersecurity_for_connected_eshunt_im.novelty_concern_pre_check: HIGHLY SATURATED — medical device cybersecurity is established discipline with regulatory standards (FDA, IEC, AAMI) + multiple existing patents.
M8_cybersecurity_for_connected_eshunt_im.advance_verdict: SATURATED — general cybersecurity methods are not patentable (Alice §101 + saturation). eShunt-specific cybersecurity is a routine engineering adaptation, not a patentable invention.
M8_cybersecurity_for_connected_eshunt_im.honest_negative_finding: M8 killed at pre-check: medical device cybersecurity is established regulatory + engineering discipline. eShunt-specific cybersecurity is routine adaptation. Cannot be patented as standalone invention.

physics_precheck_summary.leading_candidate_after_physics_precheck: M1 — Predictive failure detection via ML on chronic dual-pressure sensor data. PASSES physics. Validated precedent (CardioMEMS HF prediction AUC=0.89). eShunt-specific novelty = endovascular dual-pressure-differential ML signature + hydrocephalus failure prediction. Strongest candidate.
physics_precheck_summary.strong_alternative_after_physics_prechec: M7 — End-of-life prediction & elective replacement scheduling. PASSES physics. Must be claimed as METHOD with specific eShunt RUL signatures (dual-pressure drift pattern + biofouling indicator + sensor impedance trend) to gain novelty over generic RUL engineering.
honest_negatives_documented: M2 (post-market surveillance infrastructure) — pure software registry, §101 Alice risk + saturation
M3 (PRO integration) — pure software, Alice §101; only novel as integration with M1
M4 (fleet learning) — weak standalone; only novel as integration with M1+M5
M5 (remote programming) — saturated by Hakim programmable valve + CardioMEMS telemetry
M6 (batteryless) — CardioMEMS RF inductive powering precedent; piezo/thermoelectric fail physics
M8 (cybersecurity) — established regulatory + engineering discipline; routine adaptation
physics_precheck_summary.key_physics_insight: T10 candidates fall into TWO categories: (1) HARDWARE-DEPENDENT intelligence (M1, M7) requiring chronic sensor deployment (Position 002 dual-pressure sensor or T9 M10 biosensor); (2) PURE SOFTWARE infrastructure (M2, M3, M4, M5, M8) which faces §101 Alice risk and prior-art saturation. Only M1 and M7 survive physics pre-check with conditional novelty. Both require the eShunt to be augmented with chronic sensors — meaning T10 is INSEPARABLE from T9-adjacent hardware investment. The patentable claim space is in the ML+RUL METHOD with specific signal features (dual-pressure drift signature, sensor impedance trend, biofouling indicator) — NOT the abstract method.

M1_predictive_failure_detection.strongest_alternative: M7 (End-of-life prediction) — same data stream (chronic dual-pressure sensor), different predictive target (RUL vs acute failure event). M1 predicts WITHIN-HOURS to WITHIN-DAYS failure events (obstruction, thrombosis). M7 predicts WITHIN-MONTHS to WITHIN-YEARS elective replacement timing. They are complementary, not competitive. As separate patents, M1 is stronger because (a) clinical urgency higher (emergent vs elective), (b) ML signal richer (rate-of-change vs gradual trend), (c) buyer willingness to pay higher (avoid emergent revision).
M1_predictive_failure_detection.what_failure_can_kill_us: Three failure modes: (1) IDENTIFIABILITY — obstruction vs thrombosis vs sensor drift may be mathematically collinear in pressure signal (per #1 V24/V25 lesson — Jacobian rank < 3 latent states). V2 MUST perform Jacobian identifiability pre-check BEFORE ML training. (2) TRAINING DATA — no chronic eShunt sensor dataset exists; model training requires synthetic data or transfer learning from CardioMEMS HF dataset (different physiology). (3) HARDWARE DEPENDENCE — M1 depends on Position 002 dual-pressure sensor deployment; if Position 002 is not deployed, M1 has no data stream. The patent claim must be METHOD-level (signal features + ML + clinical action) to avoid being tied to specific hardware.
M1_predictive_failure_detection.why_worth_keeping_instead_of_replacing_w: M1 is the ONLY T10 candidate with conditional novelty AND a clear regulatory path (SaMD under FDA 510(k) with CardioMEMS predicate). M1 fills a wide-open IP gap (no CereVasc patent covers ML on chronic eShunt sensor data). M1 leverages CereVasc's existing IP (Position 002 dual-pressure sensor invention) to extend into digital health — a strategic moat expansion. M1 addresses the highest-priority clinical need in hydrocephalus (shunt revision reduction — #1 patient/caregiver burden). M1 has clear commercial path (recurring revenue from cloud-based ML service, hospital analytics dashboard).

M7_end_of_life_prediction.strongest_alternative: M1 (Predictive failure detection) — same data stream, different predictive target. M7 predicts elective replacement timing (months-years); M1 predicts acute failure events (hours-days). They share the same data infrastructure but serve different clinical workflows. If only one can be pursued, M1 wins on clinical urgency + buyer willingness.
M7_end_of_life_prediction.what_failure_can_kill_us: Three failure modes: (1) PACEMAKER ERI PRIOR ART — pacemaker Elective Replacement Indicator is FDA-required regulatory standard; broad RUL claims are not patentable. M7 must claim SPECIFIC eShunt signal features (dual-pressure drift pattern + biofouling indicator + sensor impedance trend) to gain novelty. (2) DATA SPARSENESS — eShunt chronic sensor data doesn't exist yet; RUL model requires years of multi-patient data to train. (3) HARDWARE DEPENDENCE — same as M1.
M7_end_of_life_prediction.why_worth_keeping_instead_of_replacing_w: M7 is complementary to M1 (not competitive). Together they form a TWO-TIER predictive platform: M1 = acute (within-days) failure prediction; M7 = chronic (within-months) RUL forecast. Both can be patented as separate METHOD claims sharing data infrastructure. M7 specifically addresses the eShunt's chronic implant lifespan problem (5-10+ years) which is unique to CSF shunts vs cardiac devices (pacemaker battery ERI is hardware-driven; eShunt RUL is multifactorial — biofouling + tissue ingrowth + sensor drift).
